annotations.text:
Business-user vocabulary throughout:
Collect · Parse · Transform · Filter · Store.
Each step answers one question. Filter keeps its dropped rows in a review bin — that is why it stays its own step instead of hiding inside the SQL.

Parse: everything you settled.
• Name + description back on the pane (pencil) — renaming never un-tests the step.
• Only two tabs left: Sample and Parsed. Upload / Paste / Import / Export sit on the Sample tab.
• Properties are collapsible sections, one row each, with the value the sample resolves to shown underneath. Two columns at full width. Change one and the section header counts it; the arrow resets it.
• No Options tab, no Row filter, no Files & metadata. Files → Collector step; descriptions → Transform; partitioning → Store.
• Filename column: one checkbox, on by default.

Transform — decided:
• Simple = a table that GENERATES the SQL, one row per field, five plain verbs (Keep · Remove extra spaces · UPPERCASE · Change type · Calculate). Table → SQL needs no parser.
• Advanced = the SQL itself. Edit it by hand and the step LOCKS: the table greys out until you 'start over from the table'.
• Built for 600+ columns: search, view-only filters with counts, a fixed # = output position (page 2 starts at #11), pages of 10 / 20 / 100, and a sample preview that shows only the fields on the current page.
Try it: search 'attr_01', click 'Changed', remove a field, then open Advanced and type anything into the SQL.
